title: EvoAgents: Generative AI for Rapid Architecture Search in Cell Nuclei Detection

mechanism.domainTask: CNN architecture search for cell nuclei segmentation
mechanism.populationDetail: A population of three CNN programs is maintained per generation for ten generations, with no stated island or tree structure.
mechanism.archiveDetail: The top two models become parents, but a separate persistent elite archive is not described.
mechanism.replacementDetail: The text says per-generation population of three and parent selection, but omits the exact survivor/replacement operation; Figure 2's program database is not specified as an archive.
mechanism.generationDetail: Initial CNN code is generated from the task; subsequent GA crossover combines two parent architectures and mutation changes a parent parameter or structure.
mechanism.feedbackDetail: Validation loss, Dice, and IoU are recorded; the paper calls them multi-objective fitness yet also says fitness is validation cross-entropy loss.
mechanism.parentSelectionDetail: Crossover uses both selected parents; mutation uses one; the exact simulated-annealing effect on selecting the top two is not specified.

provenance.sourcePdf: papers/EvoAgents Generative AI for Rapid Architecture Search in Cell Nuclei Detection.pdf
provenance.citationWarning: Short paper: exact survivor update, elite archive, prompt templates, GA operator-selection policy, annealing schedule, and LLM usage after initialization are not specified. Evaluation is called multi-objective but also defined by validation loss; avoid asserting an unambiguous vector objective. Current survey cites this work only under biomedical imaging.
